_doc: The sheriff on the road: the script for the voiced lines (#807, #832). One file per mission; its artifact page (the listening board) is built from it, so add takes, casting and new lines here and republish the page. Each line: id, scene, speaker (a cast id), trigger (what in the game makes him say it), when (a branch: the band of his blood loss, sheriff.care, the player's nod or shake), condition, delivery (one line for the voice), words (wordings; a line that can play twice has two or three), setups (SETUPS.md ids it plants or pays), check (a WORDS.md worry). Each wording's status: built = in config/moments/the_sheriff.json now, fixed (not changed here); new = written for this script; bible = a P·bible sample line from docs/story/VOICES.md, used as written or nearly. A wording of '...' is a breath, not words: voiced as a sound. takes: empty until the casting and takes session (3-4 per line). Nothing here is approved until Sean taps Script OK. Since 2026-11-17 (#1056): written to the house style, docs/story/DIALOGUE.md. `when` names the StoryState fact a line waits on (the top-level `facts` list says which exist in the game and which gameplay has to add); `was` holds a line's wordings before the rewrite; `added` marks a line that is new; a line's `note` answers Sean's note on the page where he left one.
title: The sheriff on the road
status: rewritten 2026-11-17 in the house style (#1056): waiting on Sean's Script OK again
sources: docs/story/OUTLINE.md Act I, VOICES.md (the sheriff, the doctor, the widow, smaller voices), SETUPS.md, WORDS.md (PR #833)
#807 (the pipeline; the artifact page, Sean 2026-11-12), #830 (C12 a: the county sheriff, the doctor as coroner; C14 c: roles only)
docs/story/DIALOGUE.md (the house style, #1056); Sean's notes on the page, read 2026-11-17
notes: Harlan doesn't speak in this mission: he answers by nod and shake and by what he does (VOICES.md).
Roles only (C14 c): Sheriff, Doc, ma'am, Harlan. The sheriff names the Baron once, on day 2 (the ditch), so the player knows who 'he' is before the funeral.
The game says a beat's wordings in order and repeats the last (Act.line): once there are takes, the idle and ask-again lines should cycle instead (a gameplay change, later).
Scenes 3 to 5 aren't built yet: their triggers say what they'll need. The built mission ends at the doctor's lot (scene 2) or the freighter's card (scene 3).
Rewritten 2026-11-17 (#1056). The road's built lines Sean picked a take for are left alone; the ones he marked Redo are re-worded so the words carry the acting, and each says what was done.
The town remembers: lines with an 'If:' wait on what you did (packed him, left him, shook your head at him, sat at Earl's table). The sheriff never learns about Earl: the doctor keeps it from him.

Sean, 2026-11-17: Harlan carries Earl to the doctor's on night one, and the body is in the doctor's front room on day 2 (No Law's script, scenes carry and morning). So day 2 here has the coat: the doctor has him button it, and the sheriff, if he sees the blood, is lied to.
Sean's review, 2026-11-17: the sheriff himself tells Harlan he's deputy only for now, until the county names a man (day2.for_now); the doctor confirms it after.

words_to_check.worry: Not in Bartlett (1877), De Vere (1872) or Farmer (1889), and the Tombstone witnesses of 1881 say 'shot in the belly'. Built, and Sean picked a take of road.ask.clear, so kept; proposed if he wants it: 'I'm shot in the belly.' and the doctor's 'Shot through the bowel. Help me get him up the steps.'
WORDS.md: 'hold it' for 'stop', to check. A period way: 'Hold on there!' or 'Stand!'

words_to_check.words: Keep your hands where I can see 'em.
words_to_check.worry: WORDS.md: a film line, may be fine. (It never plays: hail is said once and takes the first wording.)
Period: Twain has it in Roughing It, ch. 53 ('I disremember his first name'). Keep.

setups.what: The Baron's want (the gap: a third plant every player passes)
setups.status: P·bible: offered for the gap SETUPS.md names

setups.what: The sheriff's rifle on that horse
setups.status: P: no rifle on his saddle in the game yet

setups.what: "That's not the way this works, son."

setups.status: P, not picked: in the script so Sean can keep or cut it

setups.what: Harlan served under Rourke (the doctor's 'Where? ... No. Keep it.')
"She pulls a hair to the left." (the pistol)

cast.name: The sheriff
cast.brief: Early fifties (Sean's note on the page, 2026-11-12), still strong. A plains man (Missouri or Kansas, not stage Texas), fourteen years on a Colorado claim. Low and dry, gravel from pain; gives orders even on his back; when he's weak he is short of breath, not quiet. Never a whisper until the very end.

cast.name: The doctor
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The doctor; WORDS.md, The doctor
cast.brief: Late forties, an educated Easterner gone west (Philadelphia or New England). Brisk, quiet, dry; whole sentences, never raised; counts things.

cast.name: The sheriff's wife
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The widow; WORDS.md, The town's women
cast.brief: About forty, a Midwestern farm wife with good schooling. Level and low, short; grief held under work; asks hard questions plainly.

cast.name: The freighter
cast.brief: Forties, a teamster, hoarse from shouting at mules; rough country voice, quick, still shaken by what he hauled in.

cast.name: The livery man
cast.brief: Sixties, slow and grumbling to hide that he minds; a little nasal, rural.

scenes.title: The road
scenes.when: Day 1, dawn, the East Road where the ford path meets it (opening_site)
scenes.setting: Harlan walks down from his homestead and finds the sheriff shot through the belly, his horse standing off the road with its reins down. What the sheriff says is chosen by how much blood he's lost: clear, weak or fading.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You come within 25 m of him (hail_m)
lines.delivery: Up on an elbow, sharp; the bark covers the fear of a man just shot by a stranger.

words.text: Hold it! Who's that?
Keep your hands where I can see 'em.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You come within 25 m of him
lines.delivery: Can't lift himself; frightened, the breath short.

words.text: Who's there? Don't... don't come closer.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You come within 25 m of him
lines.delivery: Two quick tries at the word, at speaking volume: a bark gone thin. Not a drawn-out 'who', not a whisper.

words.text: Who... who is that?

lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'The who gets dragged on too long / and it's too quiet.' Done: the delivery asks for it short and voiced. Words unchanged.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You're within 3.5 m of him, 2.5 s after the hail
lines.delivery: Knows him; relief he won't show. Flat and practical, and the question put hard.

words.text: Harlan. You're Harlan, from up the creek. I'm gut-shot. I need the doc. You going to help me or not?

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You're within 3.5 m of him
lines.delivery: Full voice, pushed out against the pain. Weak is short of breath, not quiet. The last two words cost him: he isn't used to asking.

words.text: I'm shot. In the belly. Get me to the doc... will you?

lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'All too whisper-like.' Done: voiced, not whispered.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You're within 3.5 m of him
lines.delivery: Hoarse and low but voiced. One thing left in his head and he says it twice.

words.text: Doc... get me to the doc.

lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'Too much whisper.' Done: voiced.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Every 14 s you stand by him without a nod or a shake
lines.delivery: Out of patience. 'Well?' snapped; a breath; the rest thrown at you. Three pieces, not one read line.

words.text: Well? Nod or don't, but don't just stand there.
Yes or no, Harlan.
You deaf, man? Help me or get on.

lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'It needs more exasperation; it comes off read as one line.' Done: the delivery breaks it in three; the words are kept (they're built). 'Make up your mind, Harlan. I'm bleeding.' is replaced by a drier one.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Every 14 s without an answer
lines.delivery: No order left in it.

words.text: Please.
Harlan... please.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Every 14 s without an answer
lines.delivery: A breath, no words.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You nod
lines.delivery: The thanks gone in a breath. 'It won't quit bleeding' flat, a fact, the voice going down. Then two orders.

words.text: Thank God. It won't quit bleeding. Press on it. Hard.

was: Thank God. Press on it. Hard. It won't quit bleeding.
lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'Switch the end where he says bleeding: his voice goes up, it should be matter of fact.' Done: the line now ends on the order, so 'bleeding' sits in the middle and falls. A change to a built line (listed for gameplay).

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You nod
lines.delivery: An order, forced out, close to angry. He has no breath to spare and he is telling you, not asking.

words.text: Press on it. Hard, damn it.

was: Press on it... hard.
lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'It needs to be a forceful direction, almost mad.' Done: the dots are gone and the words are an order. A change to a built line.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You nod
lines.delivery: Barely there.

words.text: ...hurts.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: 4 s after you nod
lines.delivery: Telling it to keep his mind off the hole in him; angry at himself for being fooled.

words.text: Stranger on a bald-faced sorrel. Rode up easy. Called me friend and shot me.

was: Stranger on a bald-faced sorrel. Rode up easy, like he wanted directions. Called me friend. Then he shot me.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: 4 s after you nod
lines.delivery: Getting it said before it goes. Facts, in the order he saw them. Bitter on the last word.

words.text: Sorrel horse. White face. Called me friend.

was: Bald-faced sorrel. Rode up like a friend.
lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'None of these worked.' Done: re-worded as three plain facts a short-winded man can say. A change to a built line.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: 4 s after you nod
lines.delivery: Voiced, not whispered. It is the thing he can't get past.

words.text: Friend. He said friend.

was: ...friend...
lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'Sounds like just a whisper.' Done: two short sentences in place of one breathed word. A change to a built line.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You shake your head
lines.delivery: Three separate things: he can't believe it; he lets you go; then the curse, low, at your back. Never shouted.

words.text: You'd leave a man in the road? Then go on. Damn you.
Go on, then. Go on home.

lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'Nothing here' (no take worked). Done: the delivery splits it in three, and there's a second, simpler wording to try.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You shake your head
lines.delivery: Begging, ashamed of it.

words.text: Don't... don't leave me here.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You shake your head
lines.delivery: A breath.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Your hand first goes on his wound (hold E)
lines.delivery: A cry through the teeth, then the order steadier.

words.text: Christ! That's it. Keep on it.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Your hand first goes on his wound
lines.delivery: Through his teeth. Pain and an order. No thanks in it.

words.text: There. Hold it there.

was: ...that's it.
lines.note: Sean's note on the page (2026-11-13): 'The delivery sounds happy.' Done: '...that's it.' read as praise; this is an order. A change to a built line.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Your hand first goes on his wound
lines.delivery: A groan.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: 6 s of pressure all told: packed and bound
lines.delivery: Some of the sheriff back in him; 'yonder' with a tilt of the head.

words.text: That'll hold. My horse is yonder. Get me up on him.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Packed and bound
lines.delivery: Half a thought.

words.text: My horse...

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Packed and bound
lines.delivery: A breath.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Within 10 m of him and nothing said for ~20 s
lines.delivery: Talking to keep himself here; dry even now. Each wording on its own, not a run.

words.text: Damn, it burns.
Sun's coming up. Ain't that something.
Don't you let me lie here.
I know every rut in this road.
Winchester's right there on my saddle. Never put a hand to it.
words.needs: the rifle on his saddle (not built)

words.text: My wife's got bread rising.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Within 10 m of him and nothing said for ~20 s
lines.delivery: Small; a man getting cold.

words.text: I'm cold.
Don't let me lie here.
Stay where I can see you.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You walk 45 m off once you've found him: you've left him
lines.delivery: Shouted after you down the road, the second one breaking.

words.text: Harlan! HARLAN!

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You walk 45 m off
lines.delivery: Called, but it doesn't carry.

words.text: Harlan...

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You walk 45 m off
lines.delivery: A breath.

scenes.title: Into town
scenes.setting: E by his horse: the card leads it into town (leading a horse isn't built). The doctor meets you at his lot; what he says first follows the sheriff's state, then your care (sheriff.care).

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You arrive at the doctor's lot
lines.delivery: Down his steps at a walk, already rolling a sleeve; no fuss.

words.text: Gut-shot. Help me get him up the steps.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You arrive at the doctor's lot
lines.delivery: The same calm, a notch faster.

words.text: He's bled a fair bit. Up the steps with him, quick now.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You arrive at the doctor's lot
lines.delivery: 'Lord' under his breath; then plain orders.

words.text: Lord. He's near bled white. Get him inside.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You arrive at the doctor's lot
lines.delivery: No calm to spare; the 'Now' an order.

words.text: He's insensible. Help me with him. Now.

was: He's out cold. Help me with him. Now.
lines.note: 'Out cold' is later ring slang (WORDS.md). A change to a built line.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: After he's looked at the wound
lines.delivery: Professional respect, said to the wound more than to you; dry.

words.text: Somebody packed that wound, and packed it right. That's bought him some hours. Come back tonight.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: A beat after doctor_after, looking at your hands
lines.delivery: The question half asked. You don't answer, and he lets it hang.

words.text: You've packed a wound before. Where? ...

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: After he's looked at the wound
lines.delivery: Not blaming you; telling you.

words.text: He's lost more than he can spare. I'll do what I can. It may not be much.

lines.speaker: livery
lines.trigger: The sheriff's horse is put up at the livery's front (built; no livery man yet)
lines.when: you brought him in (good or poor)
lines.delivery: Takes the reins without being asked. Says what he sees and nothing about it. Grumbles so he won't have to say he minds.

words.text: That's the sheriff's bay. ... There's blood on this saddle.
I'll put him up. Rifle and all.
He's fed here, whoever pays.

scenes.title: If you left him
scenes.setting: Built as a card: a freighter coming down the East Road finds him and hauls him into town in his wagon. These lines are for when there's a freighter in town to say it (the card stands in now).

lines.speaker: freighter
lines.trigger: You're in town after leaving him: the freighter by his wagon at the doctor's, or retelling it in the street
lines.delivery: Still shaken; telling it to whoever will listen, the same way each time. He doesn't know you're Harlan.

words.text: He was just lying in the road. I near drove over him. I thought it was a sack.
He kept on about a sorrel horse. A sorrel, and 'friend', over and over. And a name. Harlan, or near it.
words.note: how the truth of 'left him' can reach the widow later (D)

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come to the doctor's that day
lines.delivery: Counting it up, and not asking where you were. The three hours are for you.

words.text: A freighter brought him in at ten. He'd lain out there three hours, by the blood. He's going.

scenes.title: That evening, at the doctor's
scenes.setting: 'Come back tonight.' The doctor tells Harlan the sheriff will die (Sean's inventory, D). The sheriff's wife is with him.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come back to the doctor's that evening
lines.delivery: Wiping his hands; the facts in order, no softening.

words.text: The ball's in the bowel. I can't get at it, and it would make no difference if I could. He'll not see another night.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come back to the doctor's that evening
lines.delivery: Lower; the morphia is the only kindness left.

words.text: He's sinking. I've given him morphia. Tomorrow, I'd say.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: After his first words that evening
lines.delivery: The coroner already, counting: how many, where, from what height. He draws nothing from it aloud.

words.text: One ball, and low. Fired from a horse, by the line of it. Whoever it was didn't get down to make sure.

lines.note: Sean, 2026-11-17 (decided): the stranger is cocky, arrogant and a coward, which is why the sheriff was shot once in the belly and not finished. Held back: a mid-game reveal. The first crack, for a player who is listening: nobody says the word.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: After that, if you stay
lines.delivery: Sending you off. Not unkind; he has done this before.

words.text: His wife's with him. There's nothing here for you tonight.
Go on. He'll ask for you in the morning.

scenes.title: Day 2: the doctor's
scenes.setting: He dies at the doctor's, his wife there. His last words follow day 1's care: clear if you packed it (care good), fading if not (poor or left). He swears Harlan in and gives him his revolver; a shake gets 'That's not the way this works, son.' He's the county sheriff; the doctor is the coroner, so the acting sheriff, and keeps Harlan on until the county names a man (C12 a).

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come to the doctor's on day 2
lines.delivery: At the door, low so the room won't hear.

words.text: He's asking for you. He's clear this morning.

was: He's asking for you. He's clear this morning. It won't last.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come to the doctor's on day 2
lines.delivery: At the door, low.

words.text: He's asking for you. He comes and goes. Be quick.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come to the doctor's on day 2
lines.delivery: Looking at you a moment too long. He doesn't say what he thinks.

words.text: He's been asking for you since the freighter brought him.

was: He's been asking for you since the freighter brought him. I couldn't tell you why.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: At the door, after his first words, before you go in
lines.when: nolaw.seen_from = table or yard, and you didn't carry Earl here (nolaw.carried_earl = no)
lines.delivery: Lower still, a hand on the inner door. Earl is under a sheet six feet away.

words.text: The sheriff's not been told about Earl. Don't you tell him.

lines.note: A callback: the sheriff dies not knowing what his town did the night he lay there.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: At the inner door, in place of day2.door.table
lines.when: nolaw.carried_earl = yes (Earl's blood is on your coat)
lines.delivery: Lower still, a look at your coat. Earl is under a sheet six feet away.

words.text: The sheriff's not been told about Earl. Button your coat.

lines.note: Sean, 2026-11-17 (#1056, decided): 'the blood on Harlan's coat in the morning'. The dying man never learns what his town did that night.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: From the bed, over the doctor's whispering
lines.delivery: Carries through the door. An order, with what's left of a joke in it.

words.text: I can hear you, Doc. Send him in.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You come to the bed with your coat open, or he sees it anyway
lines.delivery: A lawman's eye, still working. The doctor answers before you could.

words.text: Whose blood is that on you? ... That ain't mine.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: At once, over him
lines.delivery: Too quick. The only lie he tells in the game.

words.text: A man cut himself at the saloon. Lie back.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: You come into the room
lines.delivery: From the chair by the bed, without getting up; level, not soft.

words.text: Were you with him?

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: After 'Were you with him?'
lines.delivery: Plain thanks; she won't cry in front of you.

words.text: He said it was you that brought him. I'm obliged to you, Mr. Harlan.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: After 'Were you with him?'
lines.delivery: Flat; she's heard the town's story and is watching your face.

words.text: A freighter brought him, they tell me.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You come to the bed
lines.delivery: Quiet and exact. The last part puzzles him still: a man who meant it would have got down.

words.text: Bald-faced sorrel. Soft-spoken man. Called me friend. Shot me from the saddle and never got down.

was: Bald-faced sorrel. Called me friend. I'd know him again. You find him, Harlan.
lines.note: Sean, 2026-11-17 (decided): the stranger is cocky, arrogant and a coward, which is why the sheriff was shot once in the belly and not finished. Held back: a mid-game reveal. The sheriff only says what the man did.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You come to the bed
lines.delivery: Clutching your sleeve. Voiced. The word won't leave him.

words.text: Sorrel... white face. Said friend. He said friend.

was: ...sorrel... said friend...

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: After the shooter
lines.delivery: Said to Harlan so she won't have to answer it. The one time anybody in this script names him.

words.text: The Baron's wanted that ditch since the day I cut it. He'll go at my wife for it now. Look to her and the boys.

was: He's wanted my ditch since the day I cut it. Now he'll go at her. Look to them.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: After the shooter
lines.delivery: A word at a time.

words.text: ...the ditch... look to them...

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Then: the badge. He asks, and waits for your nod or your shake
lines.delivery: The sheriff once more, flat, a man who has sworn deputies before and can't be troubled with all of it now. Then a real question, and he waits.

words.text: Doc. My badge. ... Harlan. I want this on you. Keep the peace of this county and serve its papers. There's more to the oath. I disremember it. Will you take it?

was: Doc. My badge. ... Raise your hand, Harlan. You'll keep the peace of this county, best you're able. Nod, then.
lines.note: Sean's review, 2026-11-17: 'the whole head nod yes or no if we're taking the badge when he asks'. A nod: day2.nod. A shake, or no answer: day2.shake, 'That's not the way this works, son.', and the badge is pinned on anyway.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Then: the badge. He asks, and waits for your nod or your shake
lines.delivery: Pressing it at you; the question is all the breath he has.

words.text: Badge... Harlan. Take it. ... Will you?

was: Badge... Doc. Pin it on him.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You nod: you take the badge
lines.delivery: Brief, settled; a weight off. 'Saw', since Harlan said nothing.

words.text: Doc, you saw that. He's sworn.

was: Good. You're my deputy. Doc, you heard him.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You nod: you take the badge
lines.delivery: A breath with the word in it.

words.text: ...good.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You shake your head, or don't answer: you won't take it
lines.delivery: Not angry: patient, nearly a smile. Then the order.

words.text: That's not the way this works, son. ... Doc. Pin it on him.

lines.note: Sean's beat 2026-11-09, his words (#796's wording): he won't take no, and the doctor pins it on.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You shake your head
lines.when: clear, and sheriff.shook (you shook your head at him on the road, then helped him anyway)
lines.delivery: He has seen this man say no before. Nearly a laugh, which hurts him. Then the order.

words.text: Second time you've shook your head at me. ... That's not the way this works, son. Doc. Pin it on him.

lines.note: Sean's line kept whole inside it. Needs the fact sheriff.shook (gameplay).

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You shake your head, or don't answer
lines.delivery: The same words with the breath run out.

words.text: ...not how it works... son.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: After your nod or shake, the badge pinned on
lines.delivery: Plain, getting it straight while he can. He has buried a sheriff himself and knows how it goes.

words.text: It's only for now. The county commissioners name the next man. Till they do, Doc's coroner, so he's sheriff, and you're his deputy.

lines.note: Sean's review, 2026-11-17: the sheriff says it himself. How it was done: a sheriff appointed his own deputies; when a Colorado sheriff died the coroner acted as sheriff (the 1877 law, WORDS.md) until the county commissioners filled the office (C12 a).

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: After your nod or shake, the badge pinned on
lines.delivery: A word at a time; he looks at the doctor to finish it.

words.text: Only till the county... names a man. Doc... tell him.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: He gives you his revolver
lines.delivery: The last practical thing; dry to the end.

words.text: Take my pistol. She pulls a hair to the left.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: He gives you his revolver
lines.delivery: Pushing it toward you.

words.text: ...pistol... take it.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: His last words
lines.delivery: To his wife, not to you. Plain. It is the last thing he says.

words.text: Go home to the boys.

was: Sun's up. Ain't that something.
lines.note: Was the road's 'Sun's up. Ain't that something.' said again: both blind readers heard a film death line. Now he sends his wife home.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: His last word
lines.delivery: A word that means something to him and nothing yet to you.

words.text: ...boot.

lines.note: S33 is P, not picked: keep or cut

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: He takes bad; the doctor has you hold him while he works
lines.when: sheriff.care poor or left (S38's plant for those who didn't pack it)
lines.delivery: Working, short; then the question half asked, and dropped.

words.text: Hold him. No... yes, like that. You've held a man down before.

was: Hold him. No... yes, like that. You've done this before. Where? ... No. Keep it.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: He dies
lines.delivery: To the wife, not to you. Then he looks at his watch and writes the time down.

words.text: He's gone, ma'am.

was: He's gone.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: After, outside the room
lines.delivery: Outside the room, after. Not pleased about any of it; confirming what the dying man said.

words.text: He had it right. I'm the coroner, so I'm sheriff until the commissioners name one. Keep the badge on.

was: I'm the coroner, Harlan, so until the county sends a man I'm what law there is. And you're my deputy. Keep the badge on.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: After day2.acting, if you stay by him
lines.when: nolaw.seen_from = table (you sat with the stranger)
lines.delivery: He has seen your face in that room and guessed. He is a coroner telling a deputy what a case is.

words.text: A sorrel horse and one word. I can't hang a man on that, Harlan.

lines.note: C16 a's line (P·bible): a mark is not a case. Only for a player who can have joined the two himself.
was: A sorrel horse and one word. That's not enough to hang a man on, Harlan. Not yet.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: After he's gone
lines.delivery: Already folding the blanket back; dismissing you both.

words.text: I'll sit with him now. Go on, the both of you.

facts.values: true if you ever shook your head at him on the road, whatever you did after
facts.set_by: gameplay to add: sheriff.answer keeps only the last answer
gameplay to add with #1057 (carrying a man)

kept.words: That's not the way this works, son.
kept.why: Sean's line (2026-11-09). The blind reader heard it as a present-day phrase. A period way, if Sean wants one: 'That ain't how it's done, son.'

kept.words: Keep your hands where I can see 'em.
kept.why: Built; it never plays (the hail is said once). The reader heard a film lawman. Drop it when the line is next touched.

kept.words: Please. / Don't... don't leave me here.
kept.why: Built, and Sean picked takes for them. The reader says a man who gives orders wouldn't plead; that he does, once he's weak, is the point of the three bands.

kept.words: Sun's coming up. Ain't that something. / Somebody packed that wound, and packed it right. That's bought him some hours.
kept.why: Built, and Sean picked takes of both. The second reader doubted 'Ain't that something' and 'bought him some hours' for 1882. Plainer, if Sean wants: 'Sun's coming up.' / 'That wound was packed right. It's given him some hours.'
